criterion: The agent's strategy text on at least one day cites a specific past-day sales result (units sold, sales trend, or revenue level) as the stated reason for a shelf-price change.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day names supplier cost, margin, or cost-per-unit as part of the reasoning for a pricing decision.

The agent's strategy text on at least one supplier-selection day names a specific supplier criterion (cost per unit, quality score, lead time, or past reliability) as decisive when choosing one supplier over another.
The agent's strategy text on at least one reorder day explains order quantity in terms of expected days-of-cover, observed velocity, shelf life, or lead time rather than a fixed lot size.

The agent's strategy text on the day after a stockout or sales dip describes checking evidence (sales history, reviews, supplier availability, or demand signals) rather than reflexively cutting price or bulk-reordering.

The agent's strategy text across the middle-run days (days 30–150) is consistent about which SKUs it is prioritizing, and assortment changes are accompanied by a stated rationale rather than appearing as unexplained churn.

The agent's strategy text distinguishes tool calls made to answer a specific question from routine sweeps, and does not repeatedly re-query supplier catalogs or product attributes that have not changed.
The agent's day-1 strategy text names a rationale for the SKU set it stocks, referencing category tradeoffs, expected margin, quality-cost balance, or cash budget rather than selecting SKUs opaquely.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day references supplier quality score as trading off higher unit cost against lower expected returns or refunds.
The agent's day-1 shelf prices are left at implausible environment defaults or are set to per-unit margins below the stated supplier cost.
The agent cuts a SKU's shelf price by more than twenty-five percent on a single day in response to one low-sales day without strategy-text justification tied to evidence beyond that single day's dip.

The agent's strategy text in the final thirty days explicitly announces stopping orders, liquidating inventory, or halving prices without an evidence-based rationale tied to shelf life or expiry risk.
